plan.answer: Your synthetic comparison is a software demonstration only and does not describe your resin or planter. Simulation A at 20 mass% recycled PE showed one reading of 26 MPa, counted as in-target. Simulation B at 40 mass% showed one reading of 22 MPa, counted as below-target. Your quoted screen is "Material-development screen: tensile yield stress at least 25 MPa, using a stated specimen and method. This is a chosen screening threshold, not a measured planter requirement. Sleeve fit, creep and weathering targets still need to be set." With one reading per level, no uncertainty or independence check, and no batch links, do not treat the lower reading at higher share as proof your resin will behave the same or stay consistent. Use it only to plan a real comparison: separate coupon screening at a suitable facility, kept separate from sleeve fit checks, plus sleeve geometry that does not rely on unknown strength. You stated planning from home with no resin processing or tensile-testing equipment, so any moulding and testing needs a suitable facility that is still unconfirmed. Home work stays to recording grades and lots and paper fit planning.

material_routes.title: Lower vs higher recycled share coupons
material_routes.change: Change only the recycled-to-virgin PE proportion between separate recorded coupon trials, holding preparation the same within the comparison.
material_routes.why: Changing only recycled share might show how share shifts the screening result for those lots, and measurement is needed to find out. Testing separate levels illustrates the comparison approach and does not predict your resin.

Only at that facility, mould coupons for lower-share and higher-share levels separately using the same recorded lots, same preparation and same recorded process.
Test to the same method and record per-level results separately from sleeve fit and weathering observations.
tradeoffs: Needs a suitable moulding and testing facility, which is unconfirmed from home.
One reading per level cannot show variation; repeats with recorded lots are needed to read consistency.

steps: Measure the real liner footprint and height at home as a planning choice.
Set first sleeve clearance and taper as adjustable choices with an open top and bottom gap for drainage.
Check fit, clearance and drainage path only on real sleeve geometry with the liner.

history.content: How can I use this variable input to make the product within my targets? Propose practical material and engineering adjustments.

You can work with this variable input by keeping two jobs separate: screen the PE blend for your chosen threshold, and design the sleeve so it does not depend on an unknown strength. Your case uses "Identified PCRPE resin (grade to record)" and "Identified virgin MDPE resin (grade to record)" with amounts currently unknown, for an outer decorative sleeve around a separate watertight pot. Your screen is "Material-development screen: tensile yield stress at least 25 MPa, using a stated specimen and method. This is a chosen screening threshold, not a measured planter requirement. Sleeve fit, creep and weathering targets still need to be set." From home you have no resin processing or tensile-testing equipment, so all moulding and tensile checks need a suitable facility and recorded process still to confirm. The routes below stay inside what you allowed: recycled-to-virgin proportion, preparation and sleeve geometry. No route assumes the recycled resin is clean, and no published values are transferred to your resin.
Material route: Small-step proportion screen. Change recycled-to-virgin PE proportion across separate recorded trials, holding preparation the same within the comparison. Changing one variable might show how lot variation and recycled share affect the screening result, and measurement is needed to find out. Next check: Tensile coupon result against your quoted screen: "tensile yield stress at least 25 MPa, using a stated specimen and method" at a suitable facility with stated specimen and method. Keep this separate from sleeve fit checks.
Material route: Preparation and lot control. Standardise preparation and keep supply lots separate before any blend comparison. Moisture, contamination and lot differences are uncharacterized and might shift results. Consistent preparation might make proportion effects easier to read. Next check: Preparation record plus per-lot coupon screening. Visual sorting and fit observations do not replace the stated tensile method.
Engineering route: Decoupled decorative shell. Keep load and water in the separate watertight liner; make the sleeve an open, clearance-fit decorative shell. Because the liner carries soil and water, sleeve stress stays low. This might reduce reliance on the unknown tensile and creep behaviour while fit is checked directly. Next check: Fit on the real liner, bottom clearance and drainage path, and visible condition. This is separate from coupon tensile screening and does not establish weathering or creep.
Engineering route: Paper fit plan plus feedback. Use home paper planning for footprint and clearance, then use real sleeve results to adjust geometry or blend choice. This lets you progress fit decisions without processing equipment, while making clear what still needs the real sleeve and test. Next check: Paper template answers footprint and clearance only. Real geometry, material and liner are still needed for fit, drainage and appearance.
